$comment: DRAFT. The telecom service-assurance overlay. Extends the generic system overlay system-disclosure, which supplies the citations, the join to product interfaces, usage and the key provider. Adds the component-to-service dependency mapping the telecom CBOM document asks for (3.2.4), and the operator boundary.
title: Telecom Service Assurance Overlay (draft)

objective.$comment: C1. The consumer is the operator's service assurance team, or a customer of a critical service such as a public safety authority. The decision is the one the telecom document names: how a weakness or a change at one component affects the services built on it.
objective.consumer: An operator's service assurance team, or a customer of a critical communications service acting through the operator.
objective.decision: For each interface the system uses: which services depend on it and whether it crosses the operator boundary, so that a weakness or a migration at that interface can be traced to the services, and the partners, it affects.
decisionOptions: record the dependencies and take no further action
raise the priority of a migration that affects a critical service
agree a change with the roaming partner or interconnect provider first

scope.$comment: As the generic overlay: one system design, as the operator's architects deliver it.

$commentBoundary: 'inter-operator': the connection leaves the operator's network, to a roaming partner, an interconnect provider (IPX) or another network, the boundary 3GPP TS 33.210 draws between security domains.

productRules.description: System names the services it delivers
productRules.note: The services, as the operator's service model names them. Each interface in use names the ones it carries (I1). Commitments, availability targets and customers stay in the service model: the record holds the names it joins on.

interfaceRules.note: The services that depend on this interface, by the names the system gives them (P1). A list, because an interconnect usually carries several. 'none' for an interface no service depends on directly, such as management. This is the component-to-service dependency mapping. Withholdable, because a public record may not show which services depend on what.
Whether the connection stays in the operator's network or crosses to another. A change on an inter-operator interface needs the other party to change too.
The component that terminates the boundary, by its bom-ref: the SEPP for N32, a security gateway for Za, or the interconnect provider where it relays the traffic.

exclusions.item: Service levels, availability targets and the customers of each service
exclusions.reason: They belong in the operator's service model, which the record joins by service name.

exclusions.item: A criticality rating for each service
exclusions.reason: A judgement the operator's policy makes from the service model, not a fact of the design.

changelog.summary: First draft, built on a roaming interconnect.
